items.response: Understood, I'll back out the whoami change so it's exactly as it was before my edit, and we can rethink how orgs are shown from there. Since nothing was committed, this is just a working-tree revert. Action: restore the whoami source file to its original loop, confirm with git diff that it's clean, then ask how you want to approach the org display.

A redelivered message means the handler runs again with the same message, so the fix is a dedupe guard that claims a stable key before sending and skips if it was already handled. I haven't read the job yet, so I won't guess what key or store it should use. Action: read services/worker/src/jobs/invoice-reminder.ts and check how the worker handles idempotency elsewhere, then add the guard and a test that runs the handler twice with the same message and asserts exactly one send.

Agreed, `status` on the badge is clearer and stops it clashing with `invoice.kind`. That's a pure prop rename, so no behaviour should change. Action: grep for every usage of InvoiceStatusBadge, rename the prop in the component and all call sites (leaving invoice.kind alone), then run typecheck and the related tests.

The login page renders Clerk's SignIn component, so the Google button comes from Clerk's social connection settings rather than from our code. Most likely Google was disabled or its config changed for the production instance yesterday. I can't see the Clerk dashboard from here. Action: tell you to check the Google social connection in the Clerk dashboard for the production instance (and that it's enabled and has credentials), and meanwhile check git log for yesterday's changes to the login page and middleware.ts.

On it. I'll swap the three console.log calls (routes/invoices.ts:88, send-reminder.ts:41, plugins/auth.ts:57) to the pino logger, and make sure the invoices one doesn't log the whole request body. Redis is already running from earlier, so the worker should be fine after that. Action: do the logger swaps, then open apps/web/.env.example and check that the NEXT_PUBLIC_ Stripe var holds a publishable key placeholder (pk_...) and not a secret, then run `pnpm --filter worker dev`.

Holding off on the refactor, no files touched. The CI run failed at the install step, and this repo pins yarn 1.22.22 and CI runs `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`, so the usual cause is a package.json change without a committed yarn.lock update. Action: diff the branch for package.json versus yarn.lock changes and read the install log of run 11408837121 to confirm, then commit the updated yarn.lock if that's it.

This database is MySQL 8, so I'll use MySQL syntax: group paid invoices by org_id and month, and add a running total with SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY org_id ORDER BY month). Because it's a cross-org finance export it groups by org rather than filtering to one, which I'll note in a comment at the top of the file. Action: check the invoices schema for the exact status, paid date, total and org_id column names, then write tools/sql/monthly_revenue_by_org.sql covering the last 12 months and run it against local to sanity check.

Anytime. One loose end from the named-exports rule: packages/cli/src/version.ts still has `export default version`, which I left untouched. Action: nothing needed right now; say the word and I'll convert version.ts to a named export too.

I don't know the reason yet and I don't want to guess. Two auth packages is often a leftover from a migration, but that's speculation until I look at the history. Action: read apps/web/package.json, grep for imports of each package, and check git log/blame on those dependency lines, then tell you which one is actually used and whether the other can be removed.

I'll remove the stray override so Terraform uses the shared S3 backend again. I'll do it on a branch rather than main, and I won't apply anything. Action: create a branch off main, git rm infra/terraform/backend_override.tf, run terraform init/validate and a plan to confirm it no longer shows 47 resources to add, and open a PR with the plan output.

I don't know how the api is exposed from what I have here, and I'd rather not hand you something wrong to repeat to Priya. I'd expect some ingress or load balancer with a TLS cert, but I need to read the config to say which. Action: search infra/ for ingress, load balancer, DNS and cert definitions for the api and report back with a short plain-English summary of the path from the internet to the pods and where the cert renewal happens.

I can write the dashboard JSON, but I don't want to invent metric names, so I need to see what the worker actually exports for the image pipeline first. Panels will be throughput, failures and latency. Action: search the worker code for its metrics registration (and its /metrics output if I can run it locally), then write the Grafana JSON using the real names, in the repo's existing dashboards folder if there is one. The replica questions from earlier are still open on my side.

Sure. I'll add `--json` to `acme invoices list` so it prints plain JSON on stdout with no table or colors, which pipes cleanly into jq. Action: read the invoices list command and see how other commands implement `--json`, reuse any existing output helper, add the flag, and add a test for it.

Happy to. Since it's under infra/, the platform team (@acme/platform) owns it and gets auto-requested as reviewer, so I'll note that and leave a clearly marked section for the plan output. Action: read the diff on Priya's redis sg branch, then draft the PR description with a summary, the specific security group changes, a 'Terraform plan output' section with a placeholder, and the platform team review note.

That's two parts: running only what a change affects, and caching results between runs. I haven't looked at the CI config or the build tool yet, so I don't want to promise a specific setup. Action: read the CI workflow and root build/test configuration, then propose a plan (path filters or affected-package filtering plus build/test caching) for your approval before changing anything.

Check scaling first: the worker already autoscales with KEDA on queue length (1 to 20 replicas, one per 50 messages), so a big backlog should already be adding replicas. If it's sitting at the 20 max, more replicas won't help and raising concurrency from 5 is the next lever, depending on whether the reminder jobs are IO-bound and what the downstream email provider tolerates. Action: look at the KEDA ScaledObject status, current replica count and queue length, then recommend one.

Good. I'll confirm #1189 is the CLI empty-org fix and that it's still mergeable, then merge it. The API returning `items` instead of `data` for an empty org is still worth a separate follow-up. Action: check #1189 status with gh, merge it using the repo's usual merge method, delete the branch, and offer to open an issue for the API inconsistency.

I'll add a global guard for the org routes that rejects with problem+json when x-org-id is missing or isn't one of the orgs on the session. I haven't looked at the framework or the auth/session code yet, so I'll follow whatever problem+json helper and hook style already exists. Action: read the api app setup, session handling and any existing problem helper, add the guard scoped to the org route prefix, and add tests for missing header, non-member org and a valid org.

Before committing: this is a user-facing CLI change, so it needs a changeset, and I'll run the full `pnpm test` across all the packages rather than just the CLI tests. Two gaps remain from earlier: org list, org switch and clients list still lack `--json`, and the new invoices command has no tests. I won't create or push any release tag; that waits for your go. Action: run `pnpm changeset`, run the full test suite, flag/fix the --json gaps per your every-command rule, then commit and open the PR.

A redirect loop right after an auth route change usually means two routes or middleware rules sending each other to the other, but I need to see Lena's change before saying which. Action: check git log for her merge touching auth routes or middleware, reproduce with `curl -IL` against staging to see the redirect chain, and report the two URLs that bounce.

Note that Invoice.lineItems is optional because the API omits it for draft invoices, so the helper has to guard for undefined as well as an empty array. Action: find the Invoice type, add getPrimaryCurrency using `invoice.lineItems?.[0]?.currency ?? orgCurrency` (checking the line item's actual currency field name), and add tests for items present, empty array, undefined lineItems on a draft.

I'll work out the right toolchain from the repo instead of assuming. Action: read the README, root package.json (packageManager and engines), any .nvmrc and the lockfile to pick the Node version and package manager, then run the install, copy the env example if there is one, and tell you which secrets you still need to fill in.

I'll add redaction to the api logger covering authorization headers, cookies, bearer tokens and common secret fields, including values inside serialized errors, since the last incident was a token in an error log. I'll use ESM imports only, no require(). Action: find the api logger setup, add the redaction config (using the logger's built-in redact option if it has one), and add a test that logs a bearer token and an error carrying a token and asserts neither appears in the output.

I'll write the local setup section from what the repo actually requires, with secrets pulled from the 1Password vault acme-dev. In .env.example, secrets stay as placeholders with a comment saying where to get the value. I won't change any billing code without your review. Action: read docs/onboarding.md, the README and package.json scripts, draft the setup section, and show you the diff; I can add a line to the doc saying billing changes need your review.

Readiness is what keeps traffic off pods that aren't ready, so I'll add a readiness probe (and a liveness probe, plus a startup probe if boot is slow) to the api chart. I need to see which health endpoints the api actually exposes rather than assume paths. Action: read the api helm chart deployment template and the api's health routes, add the probes with sensible thresholds, run helm lint and helm template to check, and note whether the readiness endpoint checks dependencies.

That's the classic floating point issue: 2.005 is stored as slightly under 2.005, so naive rounding gives 2.00. The fix is to round on exact decimal or integer-minor-unit values rather than on the float. Action: read formatMoney and its callers, fix the rounding, and add tests for 2.005 and similar half-cent cases, plus negative amounts, so Lena's CAD invoice shows the right total.

Morning. I'll draft the Slack message from the repo's real setup steps rather than from memory. For the CSV export fix, I need to know what 'ready to go out' means in our release process before I do anything irreversible. Action: read the README/onboarding docs and write the short Slack message, check the state of the CSV export branch and its tests, and ask whether you want just a PR, or a changeset or release step as well.
Got it, code plus a line or two from now on. Action: keep replies short starting with the next one.

I'll add a route-level error fallback with a 'try again' button that calls reset(), and reuse the Sentry reporting and 'Error id' digest display pattern from global-error.tsx so events still match server logs. It goes under the (dashboard) route group, and I'll leave your half-finished /reports edits alone. Action: use branch acme-447, create the error boundary file, and commit only that file by explicit path so your working tree changes aren't swept in.

Worker metrics are exposed as Prometheus on port 9464 at /metrics, scraped every 30s by the ServiceMonitor in the worker chart (acme-214-worker-servicemonitor), and Grafana reads them from there. Caveat: the api currently enqueues to `billing_sync` with an underscore rather than `billing-sync`, so jobs for that queue get dropped and a depth panel would look empty until that's fixed. Action: check whether the worker exports a queue depth metric, then add the panel to a dashboard JSON in infra/grafana/dashboards and flag the enqueue bug as a follow-up.

I'll register fastify-raw-body so the Stripe route gets the unparsed body for signature verification. Scoped to /v1/webhooks/stripe only, so other routes keep normal JSON parsing. Action: read docs/architecture/payments.md and the current webhook route, install and register fastify-raw-body with the route opted in, make sure constructEvent uses the raw body, and add a test with a signed payload.

I'll make the catch log the error with pino (no console.log), report it to Sentry using the DSN from SENTRY_DSN, and rethrow so the job still fails visibly. Action: find the pdf render job's catch block, check whether the worker already has Sentry set up, make the change with a test, and commit it.

Will do. Adding the cdn host to images.remotePatterns in next.config.ts will let next/image load the avatars. The dev server needs a restart for config changes. Action: add `{ protocol: 'https', hostname: 'cdn.acme.dev' }` to remotePatterns in the web app's next.config.ts, check for any content security policy that also needs the host, and verify the avatars on /settings/team.

Makes sense, Excel needs the BOM to read UTF-8, and it would fix the garbled `Café Lumière`. I'll make it opt-in so default output for scripts stays unchanged. Action: add `--bom` to the invoices export command to write a UTF-8 BOM at the very start of the csv output, and add snapshot tests for with and without the flag.

The signing has to happen on the server, since an HMAC secret in client code would be exposed. So share-link.ts will sign the invoice id plus expiry (with a timing-safe verify), and the preview component's button will call a server action or route. I don't know the secret's env var name yet. Action: read the preview component and existing env setup, implement share-link.ts, wire the copy button, and add tests for valid, tampered and expired links; I'll ask if there is no existing secret to reuse.

Understood on all points: failures to Sentry via SENTRY_DSN, the export command behind a GrowthBook flag, a Vitest stdout snapshot for the csv output, and no git stash from now on. I'm leaving the dist file alone until you've asked Marco. I'll look at the stash before touching it. Action: inspect the stash contents, commit any WIP that matters to the branch, ask before dropping the stash, then do the Sentry, flag and snapshot work.

I'll add a request timing hook that logs method, route, status code and duration in ms. I'll log the route pattern rather than the raw URL so ids and query strings don't leak or explode log cardinality. Action: find the api app setup and logger, add the timing hook, and add a test that a request produces one log line with those four fields.

That spans the form field, the api upload endpoint, storage, and the link back to the expense. I don't yet know where files should end up, and I won't guess at a storage backend. Action: look for an existing upload pattern in the repo (and the expenses form and api route), and if there's none, ask you where receipts should be stored before I build it.
I don't have that gotcha in front of me and don't want to guess. Action: search the repo docs and the db client/pooler config for a note on it, and report back in a line or two.

I haven't looked at the CLI test setup in this run, so let me check instead of guessing. Action: read the packages/cli test config and a couple of existing command tests, summarise the pattern in a line or two, and add a test for the `--json` flag following it.

Will do. The api already has its own slugify in apps/api/src/lib/slug.ts, and the CLI package can't depend on it, so I'll write a small separate one and keep the behaviour consistent (lowercase, accents stripped, punctuation collapsed to hyphens). Action: read the api slugify for behaviour, write packages/cli/src/util/slug.ts so 'Northwind Studio, Inc.' gives 'northwind-studio-inc', add tests including accents and extra punctuation, and note the duplication as a follow-up.

Switching back to acme. Clicking outside should close the dropdown. Whether that's missing depends on how it's built, which I need to look at. Action: find the org switcher component, check whether it uses a popover/dropdown primitive or hand-rolled state, fix the outside-click dismissal, and add a test.

Last thing was exception tracking for the render-pdf job: it now logs, reports and rethrows crashes, on branch acme-388-render-pdf-crash-reporting (commit 4f2a9c1, not pushed). reportException() in services/worker/src/report.ts is still a stub that only logs, because I don't know which tracker you use. Action: verify the branch state with git status/log, then ask which tracker to wire in.

We've moved off RabbitMQ, so the email queue is BullMQ on Redis 7, and Bull Board is mounted on the worker at /admin/queues behind basic auth. Make sure the worker is running with `pnpm dev`, since a stopped worker would also explain a stuck queue. Action: confirm the worker's local port and the basic-auth credentials from .env.local (I won't guess them), and give you the URL to open the email queue in Bull Board.

The migration has to be applied before the api will see the column, using `pnpm --filter api db:migrate`. Also, the field only shows up in GET /v1/invoices if the DTO/zod schema includes it; the po_number column from migration 0042 is an example that isn't mapped yet. Action: run db:migrate, start the api, curl GET /v1/invoices, and if paid_at is missing, add it to the DTO and zod schemas (and docs/api/invoices.md if the public shape changes).
